title: Microfluidic Model to Mimic Initial Event of Neovascularization
protocol: Clean the silicon wafer 3 to 5 times with methanol and isopropanol on a spin coater as follows: first spin for 15 s at 500 rpm, then spin for 60 s at 3,000 rpm.
Transfer the silicon wafer to a hotplate preheated to 180 °C and bake the wafer for 10 min.
Remove the silicon wafer from the hotplate and cool it to room temperature.
Clean the wafer again with compressed air before proceeding with spin coating.
Apply 4 mL of SU-8 2075 photoresist to the center of the wafer.
Obtain a feature height of 70 µm on the spin coater as follows: first spin for 12 s at 500 rpm, then spin for 50 s at 2,100 rpm.
Soft bake the wafer on a hotplate as follows: first bake for 8 min at 65 °C, then bake for 20 min at 95 °C.
Remove the silicon wafer from the hotplate and cool it to room temperature before lithography.
Place a photomask onto the photoresist film.
Expose the wafer with a lithography equipment to achieve a total exposure of 200 mJ/cm².
Post expose the wafer on a hotplate as follows: first bake for 5 min at 65 °C, then bake for 20 min at 95 °C.
Remove the silicon wafer from the hotplate and cool it to room temperature before developing.
Transfer the wafer to a glass Petri dish filled with SU-8 developer (PGMEA).
Shake the dish gently along the direction of the flow channel.
Change the developer after 10 min.
Repeat step until patterns can be clearly observed.
Rinse the wafer in the developer if photoresist residue is present.
Transfer the wafer to a preheated hotplate set to 120 °C and bake it for 30 min.
Pipette 35 µL of silane onto a coverslip.
Put the coverslip along with the wafer into a desiccator and pull vacuum.
Seal the desiccator and leave the wafer under vacuum for 4 h to silanize the wafer.
Release the vacuum from the desiccator.
Remove the silanized wafer onto a preheated hotplate and bake it at 65 °C for 2 h.
Store the wafer in a clean Petri dish until required.
Combine 20 g of base agent with 2 g of curing agent in a plastic beaker.
Mix them thoroughly with a mixing rod.
Place the beaker into a desiccator and pull vacuum for 1 h to remove air bubbles in the PDMS mixture.
Pour the PDMS mixture onto the wafer in the Petri dish.
Place the Petri dish back into the desiccator, degassing for another 30 min.
Remove the Petri dish from the desiccator and place it into an 80 °C dry oven for 3 h to cure.
Carefully separate the PDMS layer from the wafer.
Cut the layer to nine chips with a scalpel according to the pattern.
Punch two hydrogel injection ports out of each chip using a 1 mm biopsy punch.
Punch four media injection ports out of each chip using a 3.5 mm biopsy punch.
Clean the punched chips with residue-free tape to remove PDMS residue.
Place the chips and nine glass coverslips into a plasma cleaner.
Treat them with oxygen plasma for 30 s to form covalent bonding on the surface.
Take out the chips and coverslips.
Attach the feature side of the chips onto the coverslips.
Place the attached chips into an 80 °C dry oven for 1 h to intensify the bonding.
Autoclave the chips before use.
Keep them sterile for the rest of the procedure.
Pipet 40 µL of 1 mg/mL poly-D-lysine (PDL) and inject it into channels in the chip from hydrogel injection port.
Incubate the chips at 37 °C for 4 h to modify the surface of the PDMS.
Pipette 200 µL of sterile water and inject it into channels in the chip from hydrogel injection port to wash out PDL.
Remove the chips into a 120 °C dry oven for 3 h to restore hydrophobicity.
Place on ice a sterile tube.
Calculate the volume of Type I collagen to be used as follows: Final volume (50 µL) x Final collagen concentration (3 mg/mL in this research) / Concentration in bottle = Volume collagen to be added.
Calculate the volume of NaOH to be used as follows: Volume collagen to be added) x 0.023 = Volume 1 N NaOH.
Prepare 50 µL of hydrogel in the tube by adding 5 µL of 10x PBS, 0.5 µL of phenol red, calculated volume of 1 N NaOH, 4 µL of 1 mg/mL Fibronectin, and calculated volume of Type I collagen.
Add the proper amount of dH2O so that the total volume reaches 50 µL.
Mix all contents in the tube thoroughly.
Pipette 2-3 µL of hydrogel for each chip and slowly inject it into the central hydrogel channel from hydrogel injection port.
Incubate the chips at 37 °C for 30 min to allow gelation.
Seal the chips into a sealed box with 1 mL of sterile water.
Store sealed chips at 37 °C for up to 24 hours if not used immediately.
Pipette 20 µL of 125 µg/mL Fibronectin into one media injection port of the cell culture channel.
Cut a pipette tip to fit the port of the cell culture channel with scissors.
Insert the cut pipette tip into the other media injection port of the cell culture channel.
Pipette out air from the cell culture channel to fill it with Fibronectin.
Incubate the chips at 37 °C for 1 hour.
Pipette 20 µL of ECM media into each media injection port after incubation.
Incubate the chips at 37 °C for 30 minutes.
Pipette out all the media from all media injection ports.
Pipette 5 µL of cell suspension into one media injection port of the cell culture channel.
Add about 4-6 µL of ECM media to the other port to adjust hydrostatic pressure and stop cell movement.
Remove the chips to the cell incubator.
Turn over the chips every 30 minutes until endothelial cells coat around the internal surface of the cell culture channel 2 hours later.
Pipette a little water on the back of the coverslip to make the chip upside down.
Insert four barbed female Luer adaptors into the media injection ports and fill with ECM media.
Remove the chips to cell incubator.
Change ECM media in Luer adaptors every 12 hours.
Take out a microfluidic sprouting chip with hydrogel injected.
Repeat steps 4.1-4.6 for barrier function assessment.
Remove all Luer adaptors from the chip.
Pipette out all media in four media injection ports.
Place the chip onto the confocal laser scanning microscope.
Pipette 5 μL of culture media containing 500 μg/mL 40 kDa FITC-dextran to one port of cell culture channel.
Capture images every 3 seconds for 30 seconds without cell lining.
Take out the microfluidic sprouting chip after HUVECs are confluent in the cell culture channel.
Repeat steps 5.3-5.5 for barrier function assessment with cells.
Capture images every 3 seconds for 30 seconds with cell lining.
Calculate the diffusional permeability coefficient using changes in fluorescent intensity over time.
Use the equation Pd = (I2 - I1) / ((I1 - Ib) · Δt) · S/d.
Set Δt as 9 seconds for calculations.
Repeat step 1 to prepare the wafer for bubble trap chip.
Cut PDMS layer to three chips according to the pattern on the photomask of the top layer.
Punch six holes on the end of inlet and outlet channels of the top layer using a 3.5 mm biopsy punch.
Punch two holes on the corresponding position of bottom layer using a 6 mm biopsy punch.
Prepare 10 g of PDMS mixture.
Pour PDMS mixture on the center of a cleaned silicon wafer.
Apply spin protocol to fabricate a 100 µm PDMS film: spin for 15 s at 500 rpm, increase speed to 1300 rpm and hold here for 45 s.
Transfer wafer to preheated hotplate set to 180 °C and bake it for 30 min.
Clean punched layers with residue-free tape to remove PDMS residue.
Place top layers and wafer into a plasma cleaner and treat them with oxygen plasma for 30 s to form covalent bonding on the surface.
Take out top layers and wafer.
Attach the feature side of top layers onto the PDMS film.
Cut the film carefully along the edge of the top layers with a needle.
Slowly separate the film from the wafer and turn over the chips to make the film side up after separation.
Place the bottom layers and attached chips into a plasma cleaner and treat them with oxygen plasma for 30 s again.
Take out bottom layers and attached chips.
Attach the bottom layers onto the PDMS film.
Align the holes on the bottom layer with the patterns on the top layer when attaching.
Place the chips into an 80 °C dry oven for 1 h to intensify the bonding.
Assemble the microfluidic control system on a clean bench.
Prepare two polytetrafluoroethylene tubes, two short silicone tubes, three long silicone tubes, one barbed female Luer adaptor, one Y type connector, and three L type connectors.
Fill the syringe with 10 mL of preheated (37 °C) ECM medium.
Preheat the medium to help release dissolved gas.
Connect a polytetrafluoroethylene tube to the syringe using a barbed female Luer adaptor.
Connect the other end of the polytetrafluoroethylene tube to a Y type connector.
Attach two long silicone tubes to the other ends of the Y type connector, one connecting to the reservoir and the other to the bubble trap chip.
Connect another long silicone tube directly to the reservoir.
Use short silicone tubes to connect all inlet and outlet holes on the top layer of the bubble trap chip.
Connect a polytetrafluoroethylene tube to the backend of the chip.
Secure the syringe onto the micro-syringe pump.
Clip two long silicone tubes into the electromagnetic pinch valve.
Switch the electromagnetic pinch valve to open the pipeline between the syringe and the reservoir.
Inject media into the reservoir using a micro-syringe pump to exhaust air in the tube.
Switch the valve again to open the pipeline between the syringe and the bubble trap chip.
Inject media to fill the liquid chamber and the backend tube of the bubble trap chip.
Take out endothelial sprouting chips from the cell incubator.
Remove Luer adaptors on the cell culture side.
Insert two pipe plugs into the hydrogel injection ports of the microfluidic sprouting chip.
Connect the backend tube of bubble trap chip to one port of cell culture channel.
Insert a T type connector to the other port and connect it to long silicone tube connected with the reservoir.
Clip the long silicone tube into the micro-peristaltic pump.
Insert an air filter to the reservoir.
Assemble the microfluidic sprouting chip to the stage top incubator.
Connect the vacuum pump to the holes in the bottom layer of bubble trap chip with a TPU tube.
Set up the circulation volume and flow rate in the custom program, which controls the micro-syringe pump and electromagnetic pinch valve simultaneously.
Measure the viscosity of the medium using a coaxial cylinder type rotational viscometer.

Calculate the flow rate across the endothelial cell culture channel using the formula τ = 6µQ / Wh², where τ is shear stress (dyn/cm²), µ is viscosity of the medium (8.8 x 10^-4 Pa•s), Q is the flow rate across the endothelial cell culture channel (ml/s), h is channel height (70 μm), and W is channel width (1,000 μm).
Manually confirm the height and width of the channel using a phase contrast microscope at 4x magnification.
Set up the flow rate of micro-peristaltic pump to prevent media spillage.
Turn on the micro-syringe pump to establish circulation control system.
Fix cells and sprouts in the microfluidic sprouting chip with 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS for 15 min.
Stain nuclei with DAPI at a ratio of 1:1000 for 10 min.
Stain cytoskeleton with TRITC phalloidin at a ratio of 1:100 for 1 hour.
Wash cells with PBS three times, each for 5 minutes.
Take confocal images of the chips in tiling mode.
Stitch confocal images using image editing software.
Count the number of fluorescent pixels of Z-projection images to quantify normalized area of sprouting.
Manually identify and label each tip of sprouts in Z-projection images.
Calculate distances between sprout tips and ECs basement membrane to quantify average sprout length and longest sprout length.
